before_conditions: BuilderWallet is deployed and serves as the fee recipient for builder split commissions
BuilderWallet exposes an external init(address _builderAdmin) function that writes builderAdmin with no access control and no one-time initialization guard
BuilderWallet exposes a sweep(address token, address to) function that lets the current builderAdmin transfer the wallet's full token balance
The protocol can route commissions to riskParameters.feeRecipient(), which is the BuilderWallet address, during option mint/burn settlement
In CollateralTracker.settleMint, when riskParameters.feeRecipient() != 0, shares are split and transferred to both riskEngine() and feeRecipient
In CollateralTracker.settleBurn, when riskParameters.feeRecipient() != 0, shares are split and transferred to both riskEngine() and feeRecipient
Builder fees (shares/tokens) may accumulate in the BuilderWallet
required_property: Only an authorized party should be able to set or change builderAdmin, and builderAdmin should remain the legitimately designated builder authority so that accumulated builder fees in BuilderWallet are protected from unauthorized takeover at all times
bad_outcome: Any attacker can call init(attacker) to overwrite builderAdmin and then call sweep(token, attacker) to drain the wallet's full token balance, stealing accumulated builder fees permissionlessly and causing direct loss of funds intended for builders and any downstream accounting or fee distribution relying on this mechanism
